# Purpose {.unnumbered .unlisted}

- Check whether the assignment and randomization procedure used in the coordination analysis produces coordination when there is none (false positives)
- Check that it detects coordination when it exists (positive control)

:::

# Rationale {.unnumbered .unlisted}

In the real data callers are unknown. Overlapping series are assigned to different birds and the remaining series are assigned at random (`test_coordination_impute()`). Two features of this procedure could bias coordination scores even if the birds called independently:

1. Overlapping series are always assigned to different birds, so every imputed data set keeps all the observed overlaps
2. Non-overlapping series are assigned at random, which mixes the calling rhythms of the two birds before the randomization step

Here we simulate pairs of birds, label the series exactly as in the real data and run the same analysis. Each simulated pair is based on one real window: it has the same number of series, the same series durations and the same time span.

Three scenarios are simulated:

* **Independent (uniform)**: each bird calls at random times within the window, independently of its partner
* **Independent (shared activity)**: each bird calls independently, but both follow the window's real activity profile (start times are sampled from the real start times of the window and jittered with a normal distribution, SD = 5 min). This mimics two birds that respond to the same external cue (e.g. sunrise) without responding to each other
* **Coordinated (positive control)**: bird 1 calls at random times. Each series of bird 2 has a 50% probability of being a response, starting between 2 s before and 5 s after the start of a randomly chosen series of bird 1; otherwise it is placed at random

The true proportion of series produced by each bird is set to 50/50 or 30/70. The labelled data are analysed assuming three proportions (`prob` = 0.1, 0.3 and 0.5).

Under no coordination, about 50% of the scores should fall on each side of 0 and about 5% of the tests should be significant (p < 0.05).

# Load packages {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```{r load packages}

# install/ load packages
sketchy::load_packages(
  packages = c("warbleR", "readxl", "ggplot2")
)

source("./scripts/test_coordination_impute.R")
source("~/Dropbox/R_package_testing/warbleR/R/internal_functions.R")

```

# Read and format data

Same as in the coordination analysis.

```{r}

dat <- readxl::read_excel("./data/raw/Water rail database v4.xlsx")
dat <- as.data.frame(dat)
dat$sing.event <- paste(dat$No., dat$`Before dawn (0), after dawn (1)`, sep = "-")
dat$start <- as.numeric(dat$`Call series begin time (s)`)
dat$end <- as.numeric(dat$`Call series end time (s)`)

# windows used as templates (at least 4 series, so each bird can have 2)
n_series <- table(dat$sing.event)
windows <- names(n_series)[n_series >= 4]

length(windows)

```

# Simulation settings

```{r}

# number of simulated pairs per real window
n_rep <- 20

# true proportion of series produced by bird "a"
true_props <- c(0.5, 0.3)

# assumed proportions used in the analysis ('prob')
probs <- c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5)

scenarios <- c("null_uniform", "null_shared", "coordinated")

# test settings (reduced from the real analysis: 100 imputations x 1000 randomizations)
imputations <- 20
iterations <- 200
parallel <- 20

# SD (s) of the jitter for the shared activity scenario
jitter_sd <- 300

# positive control: probability that a series of bird 2 is a response and its lag (s)
p_resp <- 0.5
resp_lag <- c(-2, 5)

out_dir <- "./data/processed/null_simulation"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

```

# Simulation functions

```{r}

# simulate the series of one bird without self-overlap
# starts_pool: if supplied, start times are sampled from it and jittered
sim_bird <- function(n, durs, from, to, starts_pool = NULL, jitter = jitter_sd, max_tries = 1000) {
    for (k in seq_len(max_tries)) {
        d <- durs[sample.int(length(durs), n, replace = TRUE)]
        if (is.null(starts_pool)) {
            s <- stats::runif(n, from, to - d)
        } else {
            s <- starts_pool[sample.int(length(starts_pool), n, replace = TRUE)] + stats::rnorm(n, 0, jitter)
            s <- pmin(pmax(s, from), to - d)
        }
        o <- order(s)
        s <- s[o]
        d <- d[o]
        if (all(s[-1] >= (s + d)[-n])) return(data.frame(start = s, end = s + d))
    }
    NULL
}

# simulate bird 2 responding to bird 1 (positive control)
sim_responder <- function(n, b1, durs, from, to, max_tries = 1000) {
    for (k in seq_len(max_tries)) {
        d <- durs[sample.int(length(durs), n, replace = TRUE)]
        s <- stats::runif(n, from, to - d)
        resp <- stats::runif(n) < p_resp
        s[resp] <- b1$start[sample.int(nrow(b1), sum(resp), replace = TRUE)] + stats::runif(sum(resp), resp_lag[1], resp_lag[2])
        o <- order(s)
        s <- s[o]
        d <- d[o]
        if (all(s[-1] >= (s + d)[-n])) return(data.frame(start = s, end = s + d))
    }
    NULL
}

# simulate a pair using a real window as template
simulate_pair <- function(W, scenario, true_prop) {
    n <- nrow(W)
    n1 <- max(2, round(n * true_prop))
    n2 <- max(2, n - n1)
    from <- min(W$start)
    to <- max(max(W$end), from + 60)
    durs <- W$end - W$start
    pool <- if (scenario == "null_shared") W$start else NULL

    b1 <- sim_bird(n1, durs, from, to, starts_pool = pool)
    if (is.null(b1)) return(NULL)

    b2 <- if (scenario == "coordinated") {
        sim_responder(n2, b1, durs, from, to)
    } else {
        sim_bird(n2, durs, from, to, starts_pool = pool)
    }
    if (is.null(b2)) return(NULL)

    b1$true.indiv <- "a"
    b2$true.indiv <- "b"
    Y <- rbind(b1, b2)
    Y[order(Y$start), ]
}

# hide caller IDs as in the real data: overlapping series are labelled
# alternately "a" and "b" in order of start time, the rest are left as NA
label_like_real <- function(Y) {
    ov <- outer(Y$start, Y$end, "<") & outer(Y$end, Y$start, ">")
    diag(ov) <- FALSE
    is_ov <- which(rowSums(ov) > 0)
    Y$indiv <- NA_character_
    Y$indiv[is_ov] <- rep(c("a", "b"), length.out = length(is_ov))
    Y
}

```

# Simulate data

One data set per scenario and true proportion, each with `n_rep` simulated pairs per real window. The same data sets are used for all assumed proportions and both coordination metrics.

```{r}
#| eval: false

grid_sim <- expand.grid(scenario = scenarios, true_prop = true_props, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(grid_sim))) {
    set.seed(100 + i)
    sims <- list()
    for (w in windows) {
        W <- dat[dat$sing.event == w, ]
        for (r in seq_len(n_rep)) {
            Y <- simulate_pair(W, grid_sim$scenario[i], grid_sim$true_prop[i])
            if (is.null(Y)) next
            Y <- label_like_real(Y)
            Y$sing.event <- paste0(w, "_r", r)
            Y$window <- w
            Y$rep <- r
            sims[[length(sims) + 1]] <- Y
        }
    }
    sims <- do.call(rbind, sims)
    saveRDS(sims, file.path(out_dir, paste0("sim_", grid_sim$scenario[i], "_", grid_sim$true_prop[i], ".RDS")))
}

```

# Run coordination tests

Each simulated data set is analysed with the 3 assumed proportions, for both metrics. Results are saved per run, so the loop can be resumed if interrupted. As in the real analysis the p-value for time lapse tests whether birds call closer in time than expected (`less.than.chance = TRUE`). For overlap counts it tests whether birds overlap more than expected (`less.than.chance = FALSE`).

```{r}
#| eval: false

warbleR_options(pb = FALSE)

grid_run <- expand.grid(
    scenario = scenarios,
    true_prop = true_props,
    method = c("time.closest", "count"),
    prob = probs,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(grid_run))) {
    g <- grid_run[i, ]
    out_file <- file.path(out_dir, paste0("res_", g$scenario, "_", g$true_prop, "_", g$method, "_", g$prob, ".RDS"))
    if (file.exists(out_file)) next

    sims <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, paste0("sim_", g$scenario, "_", g$true_prop, ".RDS")))

    X <- sims[, c("sing.event", "indiv", "start", "end")]
    res <- suppressWarnings(test_coordination_impute(
        X = X,
        prob = g$prob,
        id = "a",
        imputations = imputations,
        iterations = iterations,
        ovlp.method = g$method,
        less.than.chance = g$method == "time.closest",
        parallel = parallel,
        seed = 123
    ))

    res <- attr(res, "imputation.results")
    res <- cbind(g[rep(1, nrow(res)), ], res, row.names = NULL)
    saveRDS(res, out_file)
}

```

# Results

```{r}

res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(list.files(out_dir, pattern = "^res_", full.names = TRUE), readRDS))
res <- res[!is.na(res$coor.score.bounded), ]

res$rep <- as.numeric(sub(".*_r", "", res$sing.event))

# score in the direction of coordination (time lapse < 0, counts > 0)
res$coordinated <- ifelse(res$method == "time.closest", res$coor.score.bounded < 0, res$coor.score.bounded > 0)

res$metric <- ifelse(res$method == "time.closest", "Time lapse", "Overlap counts")
res$metric <- factor(res$metric, levels = c("Time lapse", "Overlap counts"))
res$scenario <- factor(res$scenario, levels = scenarios, labels = c("Independent (uniform)", "Independent (shared activity)", "Coordinated"))
res$prob <- factor(res$prob, levels = probs)
res$true_prop <- factor(paste0(res$true_prop, "/", 1 - as.numeric(res$true_prop)))

```

## Real data reference

Proportion of scores in the direction of coordination in the real data for the same assumed proportions.

```{r}

real <- lapply(c(time.closest = "time_lapse", count = "counts"), function(f) {
    l <- readRDS(paste0("./data/processed/coordination_scores_by_id_proportion_", f, ".RDS"))
    all_probs <- seq(0.1, 0.5, by = 0.05)
    do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(l), function(i) data.frame(prob = all_probs[i], score = l[[i]]$coor.score.bounded)))
})

real <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(real), function(m) {
    X <- real[[m]][!is.na(real[[m]]$score), ]
    X$coordinated <- if (m == "time.closest") X$score < 0 else X$score > 0
    X <- aggregate(coordinated ~ prob, X, mean)
    X$metric <- if (m == "time.closest") "Time lapse" else "Overlap counts"
    X
}))

real <- real[round(real$prob, 2) %in% probs, ]
real$metric <- factor(real$metric, levels = c("Time lapse", "Overlap counts"))
names(real)[2] <- "real_proportion"
real

```

## Proportion of scores in the direction of coordination

Each point is one replicate (all windows and imputations of a simulated set). The dashed line marks the 50% expected without coordination and the red line the mean value in the real data across the assumed proportions.

```{r, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7}

prop_rep <- aggregate(coordinated ~ scenario + true_prop + metric + prob + rep, res, mean)

real_mean <- aggregate(real_proportion ~ metric, real, mean)

ggplot(prop_rep, aes(x = prob, y = coordinated, fill = true_prop)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, lty = 2) +
    geom_hline(data = real_mean, aes(yintercept = real_proportion), col = "red2", lwd = 0.8) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.6) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8), size = 0.8, alpha = 0.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#A0DFB9FF", "#3E4A894D")) +
    facet_grid(metric ~ scenario) +
    ylim(c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = "Assumed proportion of calls of individual 1 (prob)", y = "Proportion of scores\nin the direction of coordination", fill = "True proportion\n(bird 1 / bird 2)") +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")

```

## Summary table

`coordinated`: proportion of scores in the direction of coordination. `significant`: proportion of tests with p < 0.05 (the false positive rate in the independent scenarios and the power in the coordinated one). `median_score`: median bounded coordination score.

```{r}

summ <- aggregate(cbind(coordinated, significant = p.value < 0.05, median_score = coor.score.bounded) ~ metric + scenario + true_prop + prob, res, function(x) c(mean = mean(x), median = median(x)))

summ <- data.frame(
    summ[, c("metric", "scenario", "true_prop", "prob")],
    coordinated = round(summ$coordinated[, "mean"], 3),
    significant = round(summ$significant[, "mean"], 3),
    median_score = round(summ$median_score[, "median"], 3)
)

summ[order(summ$metric, summ$scenario, summ$true_prop, summ$prob), ]

```

## Real data compared with the independent scenarios

Proportion of simulated replicates with a proportion of scores in the direction of coordination at least as high as in the real data (pooling the assumed proportions 0.1, 0.3 and 0.5). Values close to 0 indicate that the real result is unlikely under independent calling.

```{r}

null_rep <- prop_rep[prop_rep$scenario != "Coordinated", ]
null_rep <- merge(null_rep, real_mean, by = "metric")

aggregate(cbind(as_extreme = coordinated >= real_proportion) ~ metric + scenario, null_rep, mean)

```

# Takeaways {.unnumbered .unlisted}

- **Overlap counts are robust**: independent pairs rarely overlapped, so only 2–11% of their scores were positive and 1–8% of the tests were significant, regardless of the assumed proportion. In the real data 84–86% of the scores were positive, which no independent replicate reached. The positive control gave 79–82% positive scores, so the method detects coordination when it exists
- **Time lapse is biased towards coordination by the assignment and by shared activity**:
    - With uniform independent calling, 55% of the scores were negative and 8% of the tests were significant when assuming equal contributions (0.5/0.5), slightly above the expected 50% and 5%
    - Assuming a very unequal contribution inflates negative scores (68% negative and 13% significant at 0.1/0.9)
    - Two independent birds that follow the same activity profile produce more negative scores (70–76% negative and 14–21% significant), probably because the randomization does not keep the temporal clustering of calls within the window
- **The real time lapse result is still stronger than expected under independence**: the real data had 77–86% negative scores (81% on average), similar to the positive control (83–91%). Only 1.7% of the replicates with independent birds following a shared activity profile, and none with uniform calling, reached the real value. However, the baseline for independent calling is 55–76% rather than 50%, so the time lapse result should be interpreted against this baseline and is weaker evidence than the overlap counts
